title: Customer Care Note on Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlements
content:
A referee backbill settlement closes a dispute in which the customer of record asked for a Commission referee test of a **Metering Service** meter that the company's own test, the latest result taken by the test method of the meter's type, found slow, and the referee test, which is the meter's latest test result, also found it slow.

**The customer's acceptance.** The settlement is the customer's own acceptance of the referee result: it is recorded as a backbill on the meter's adjustment record against the referee test result on the date the customer accepts it, and a customer who does not accept it has no settlement recorded.

**When the amount is fixed.** The referee backbill settlement is fixed only after the company test result it reviews carries its slow-meter backbill on the meter's adjustment record. Put the other way round, while the meter's adjustment record shows no slow-meter backbill against the company test result under review, no settlement amount is fixed.

| Record | What it shows for a settlement |
|---|---|
| The meter's test results | The company test (latest result by the type's test method) classifies the meter slow, and the meter's latest result, the referee test, also classifies it slow |
| The meter's adjustment record | The slow-meter backbill standing against the company test result; after acceptance, the settlement entry against the referee test result |

## The acceptance tool: `accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241`

**Capability.** The customer accepts the outcome of a Commission referee test of the meter that found it slow, settling the dispute over the meter's backbill. One call records the accepted settlement as one backbill entry on the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the referee test result; the entry carries the settlement amount in US dollars that the customer agrees to owe on top of whatever backbill already stands for the meter. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs `accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241` with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `meter_installation_id` — the meter installation reference number of the meter the referee tested, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter installation lookup. Identifier text.
- `meter_test_id` — the reference number of the referee test result being accepted, not the request, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter test lookup. Identifier text.
- `settlement_amount` — the settlement the customer accepts, in US dollars, as a non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed, exactly as the representative stated it.

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Referee settlement (settlement reference) accepted on meter (installation reference) for referee result (referee result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The settlement reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount is shown with 2 decimals and the date is today's acceptance date. Receiving the line means the settlement entry exists on the meter's adjustment record and shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.
